problem: Yahoo's board thought the offer undervalued the company.
title: Yahoo rejects Microsoft's $44.6 billion takeover offer
context: Microsoft offered $31 a share, a 62 percent premium, on 1 February 2008.
decision_made: Reject the offer on 11 February 2008, and later hold out for $37 a share when Microsoft raised its bid to $33.
action_taken: Co-founders Jerry Yang and David Filo told Microsoft's CEO the company would not sell for less than $37.
observed_outcome: Microsoft withdrew in May 2008. Yahoo shares fell about 14 percent the next trading day and were near $20.89 by the end of June.
lessons: Rejecting a large premium offer carries the risk that the share price never returns to that level.
limitations: The outcome compares share prices only and does not assess what a deal would have meant. Carol Bartz's later role was not covered by these sources.

claims.claim_text: Yahoo's board rejected Microsoft's $44.6 billion offer on 11 February 2008, calling it an undervaluation.
Yahoo shares fell sharply when Microsoft withdrew its bid in May 2008.
